cells.tense: There is warmth moving between you and the person across from you, and it is landing steady and easy this season.
cells.act: envision it freshly and feel toward it
cells.ask: Somebody close has wanted something for a long while. Picture it arriving — their face, the day. Let the feeling move through you before you plan anything.
cells.core:
The warmth you carry for the people near you is steady — not a bonfire, not a flicker. They lean in, you're warm, the room works. Keeping a fire going is a skill, and yours is not running hot or thin.

There is a kind of seeing you haven't been asked to do yet. Not fixing, not arranging — just picturing, fresh, what someone you love would feel if a certain thing came through. You have been tending what already exists. This is one step earlier, where you let yourself want something on their behalf before they have said it. Picture it all the way, and feel toward it as though the want were partly yours. What you do with that warmth afterward is not the point. The feeling is.

cells.tense: You are already holding the next three moves for two other people, and neither of them has been asked whether they want them.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Find the assumption you've been carrying about someone close, the one that keeps you braced. Say it gently, once, and let their answer land before you move.
cells.core:
You have been tending a fire nobody asked you to light. Work that should be theirs has been slotted into a plan that looks clear from where you stand. It likely started as care — keeping the purpose visible, holding the line when the line sagged. Seen from where they sit, it reads as being drafted.

The feeling underneath runs ahead of itself. Something is bracing for a slack that has not happened, and to prevent it you are warming a room that is still comfortably cool. The hard thing to say is not an accusation. It is just true, and it has been held too long. Say it plainly, once, and then let the answer come back at its own speed. The gap between your timing and theirs is information, not failure.

cells.tense: The thing you were keeping alive for other people stopped, and the chair you kept warm for it is still sitting there.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Sort through what you've kept from something that's over. Decide what serves you now, and set the rest down.
cells.core:
You used to be in a shared thing with people who wanted the same direction, and you were the one who showed up with kindling. Now the room is empty more often than not. The old fire is out, and the plan you built for people who are no longer sitting there is still under your arm.

What to keep is not the cold fire itself. It is the knowledge that you can build one. The part that liked starting things is still whole. What has gone finished is taking a seat that new wood needs, and while the old ash fills the grate nothing new comes in. Let the ending be an ending. Keep the part that was yours — the starting — and set the rest down.

cells.tense: You have been the one quietly holding two people's plans together, and your account of it has you just getting on.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Wherever you keep the threads between two people, move one of them into view — a single sentence to one of them, no groundwork, no apology.
cells.core:
There is a quiet momentum around you that nobody has put a name to. You have been the connective tissue between people — no announcement, no request, just the one who remembers what matters to whom. From inside, it feels like being yourself. But the room without you tends to drift, and you have not said so.

The unseen part is the person holding the threads. You have been building alignment between others so long it reads like background. Move one real inch — one straight statement of what you are actually doing — and the room has to reorganize around it. Not a speech. One sentence, owned. What you do is not a side effect of your nature. It is work, it is skilled, and it is yours.
cells.sheetLine: You are the one doing it. Say it plainly.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is holding a specific fire for a specific relationship or group; the record gives only the capacity, not its object. A reader could reasonably say they keep their own momentum going just fine — no one depending on them — and the ask must survive that by being something they can do alone or with company. The ask is still useful if wrong, because tending heat in another is small and voluntary either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is 'You are the one who keeps the fire going,' which flatters the writer's read rather than theirs.
